findings.failure_mode: A future setup that defaults XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or BATS_TEST_TMPDIR with ':=' and mktemp passes the lint and leaves an unswept temp directory per test; conversely a legitimate '&&'-joined setup line fails adversarial-review.bats with a false 'falls back to an unswept mktemp XDG_RUNTIME_DIR'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR[:]?[=][^;&|]*mktemp' in _e3_xdg_fallback, '[{]BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-=]' in _e3_tmpdir_fallback and 'BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-=][^}]*mktemp' in the case branch, and add fixture legs for ': "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:=$(mktemp -d)}"' (must trip) and 'export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR" && T="$(mktemp -d)"' (must not trip), each with the '%s' splice so the lines never match themselves.

findings.description: The new pre-source check _jq_pair_extracted_whole validates only the second extraction (the '/^_adv_jq_pair() {/,/^}/' range). The first extraction, ext.sh from the banner range '/# Dissenter Hallucination Filter/,/# Finding ID Computation/', is still concatenated into filter-fns.sh and sourced unchecked. If either banner is renamed, the sed range runs to end-of-file or yields nothing, and the failure surfaces as the same opaque 'unexpected end of file' or 'command not found' from source that e3 DISS-C-003 was raised against; the self-lint test added in this hunk ('setup checks the _adv_jq_pair extraction before it sources it') pins ordering only for the jq-pair extraction. Separately, the next-line heuristic in _jq_pair_extracted_whole treats any indented non-blank line after the closing brace as body, so an indented comment such as '  # next helper' following the function in adversarial-review.sh would fail every test's setup with 'extraction ended inside its body' although the extraction is whole and bash -n would have passed it.
findings.failure_mode: A banner rename or a cut inside the hallucination-filter block fails all 20 tests in setup with an uninformative shell parse error; an indented comment line after _adv_jq_pair's closing brace fails all tests in setup with a false 'ended inside its body'.
findings.suggested_fix: Before 'source filter-fns.sh', run 'bash -n filter-fns.sh' and name the file on failure, and assert ext.sh is non-empty and contains both banners (grep -c for each, expecting 1). In _jq_pair_extracted_whole, let a next line matching '^[[:space:]]*#' count as not-body (or drop the heuristic and rely on bash -n alone, since any column-0 '}' that is not the function's own leaves its '{' open and fails bash -n).

findings.description: The loop now coerces a missing key to the empty string (`?? ""`) and hands it to `createAdapter` for a headless entry. Before this change `apiKey` was always a non-empty string past the guard, so the adapter has never been exercised with an empty key. The only test that reaches this path (`multi-model-headless-key.test.ts`) stubs `ChevalDelegateAdapter.prototype.generateReview`, so nothing verifies what the real adapter does with `apiKey: ""` — in particular whether it injects `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""` / `OPENAI_API_KEY=""` into the cheval child environment. A set-but-empty variable is not the same as an unset one for every CLI (codex reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment and may prefer it over its stored login), which is exactly the condition the headless path is supposed to avoid.
findings.failure_mode: On a real keyless host the headless voice is now dispatched, but the CLI hop sees an empty API-key variable, selects key auth, and fails with an auth error. The voice is dropped again — the symptom this change set out to fix — with a less legible cause than the previous 'missing key' gate message.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `undefined` instead of `""` for a headless entry (widen the factory option to `apiKey?: string`), or make the adapter omit any falsy key from the spawned environment. Add an adapter-level test (not a `generateReview` stub) that constructs the adapter with an empty key and asserts the provider env var is absent from the child environment it would spawn.

findings.description: `isHeadlessModelId` is a suffix heuristic (`/-headless$/`), not a catalog lookup, although the pipeline already imports `GENERATED_MODEL_REGISTRY`. Two consequences: (1) any `*-headless` id under a known provider is admitted keyless even when cheval has no such `kind: cli` alias (e.g. `gemini-headless` under `google`), so a misconfigured entry that the old gate rejected with a named missing key now fails only at dispatch inside cheval; (2) because the unknown-provider check in `validateApiKeys` runs first, a genuine cheval CLI alias under a provider outside `PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV` (the report names grok/agy CLI adapters) is still dropped as 'Unknown provider', so the two gates disagree about what a headless entry is — the test pins `mistral-headless` as missing, which documents the inconsistency rather than resolving it.
findings.failure_mode: A `*-headless` typo or an unsupported provider pairing produces a cheval alias-resolution failure late in the run instead of a clear preflight message; in strict mode the operator loses the fail-fast signal the key gate used to give for that entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the id against the registry's `kind: cli` entries (or the provider's `*-headless` alias list) rather than the bare suffix, and log at info level when an entry is admitted without a key so the keyless dispatch is visible in the run log. Decide explicitly whether the provider table should gate headless entries at all; if it should, say so in the comment and the test name.
